findings.title: Invoke the commit callback on the consumer thread
findings.body: The commit callback is invoked from the new background commit thread. Arroyo's StreamProcessor commit callback stages and commits offsets through KafkaConsumer, whose operations must run on its consumer thread. This can fail thread-affinity checks instead of committing offsets; the exception is merely logged and retried indefinitely. Collect completed offsets in the workers, but invoke the callback from poll() on the processing thread.

findings.title: Create a fresh queue pool for each processing strategy
findings.body: The factory creates one queue pool and passes it to every strategy, but closing or terminating a strategy shuts that pool down. StreamProcessor recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so the next strategy receives stopped workers and shut-down queues. Submissions then fail in queue.put(), and submit() catches those failures and marks their offsets complete, allowing unprocessed messages to be committed. The pool and its offset tracker need a lifecycle scoped to the strategy rather than being reused after shutdown.

findings.title: Bound queued work and apply backpressure
findings.body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() never rejects work or otherwise slows ingestion. If a worker is slow or processing throughput falls below Kafka ingestion throughput, queued messages grow without bound. A slow outstanding offset also prevents the tracker from releasing later completed offsets for that partition. This can exhaust consumer memory instead of applying the documented backpressure. Bound the pending work and use Arroyo's backpressure mechanism when capacity is exhausted.

findings.title: Drain accepted work before ending graceful shutdown
findings.body: close() stops the commit thread before waiting for processing, then pool.shutdown() sets every worker's shutdown flag before the queues are drained. Workers therefore abandon queued items after their current item, and completions occurring after the commit thread exits receive no final commit. Moreover, worker.join(timeout=5.0) can return while a result processor is still running, so strategy.join() can finish while old workers continue mutating subscription state after partition reassignment. Separate graceful close/join from termination: drain accepted work, wait within the supplied timeout, and commit the completed offsets before declaring the strategy joined.
